units.zh: 南齊書卷十六‧志第八百官
units.en: Volume 16 Treatises 8: Official Posts
units.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 16 — Treatise 8: Hundred Officials

units.zh: 建官設職，興自炎昊，方乎隆周之冊，表乎盛漢之書。
units.en: The founding of offices began with the sage-kings of antiquity; it shows in the Zhou archives at their zenith and stands written in the Han histories at their flood.
units.literal: Establishing offices and setting posts arose from Yanhao; it appears in the registries of flourishing Zhou and is set forth in the books of Han at its height.

units.zh: 存改回沿，備於歷代，先賢往學，以之雕篆者衆矣。
units.en: Kept, revised, and handed down through every dynasty, it drew generations of scholars—countless hands have cut it into stone and brush.
units.literal: Preserved, altered, and carried forward, complete in successive ages; sages of old studied it, and many have carved it into writing.

units.zh: 若夫胡廣舊儀，事惟簡撮，應劭官典，殆無遺恨。
units.en: Hu Guang's Old Protocols compress the record to essentials; Ying Shao's Official Canon leaves little wanting.
units.literal: As for Hu Guang's Old Protocols, the matters are only briefly excerpted; Ying Shao's Official Canon leaves scarcely any regret.

units.zh: 王朗奏議，屬霸國之初基；
units.en: Wang Lang's memorials date to the first laying of a hegemon's foundations;
units.literal: Wang Lang's memorials and proposals belong to the founding of a hegemonic state;

units.zh: 陳矯增曹，由軍事而補闕。
units.en: Chen Jiao's supplements to the Cao Wei roster grew out of war and patched what was missing.
units.literal: Chen Jiao's additions to the Cao offices came from military affairs to fill gaps.

units.zh: 今則有《魏氏官儀》、《魚豢中外官》也。
units.en: Today we have the Wei House's Official Protocols and Yu Huan's Central and Outer Officials.
units.literal: Now there are the "Official Protocols of the Wei House" and Yu Huan's "Central and Outer Officials."

units.zh: 山濤以意辯人，不囗囗囗。
units.en: Shan Tao read men by intuition; the text is lost.
units.literal: Shan Tao judged men by his own sense, not [lacuna] [lacuna] [lacuna].

units.zh: 荀勗欲去事煩，唯論并省。
units.en: Xun Xu wanted to cut the clutter of detail and speak only of consolidation.
units.literal: Xun Xu wished to strip away transactional tedium and discuss only merger and reduction.

units.zh: 定制成文，本之晉令，後代承業，案爲前准。
units.en: Once rules were cast as written law they rested on the Jin code; later courts took up that work and made it their precedent.
units.literal: Fixed regulations made into written law take the Jin statutes as foundation; later generations inherit the enterprise and treat them as prior standards.

units.zh: 肇域官品，區別階資，蔚宗選簿梗概，欽明階次詳悉，虞通、劉寅因荀氏之作，矯舊增新，今古相校。
units.en: When the hierarchy was first drawn, grades and ranks were sorted apart: Fan Ye's register sketches the frame, the Qinming text fills the ladder; Yu Tong and Liu Yin, following the Xun family's books, bent the old into the new—ancient and present set side by side.
units.literal: At the inception official grades were delimited and ranks distinguished; Fan Ye's Selection Register gives the outline, the Qinming ranks in full detail; Yu Tong and Liu Yin, building on the Xun clan's work, rectified the old and added the new—past and present compared.

units.zh: 齊受宋禪，事遵常典，旣有司存，無所偏廢。
units.en: Qi took the throne from Song by abdication and kept the usual forms; where an office already stood, none was singled out for abolition.
units.literal: Qi received Song's abdication; affairs follow the regular code; since the relevant offices exist, nothing was especially abolished.

units.zh: 其餘散在史注，多已筌拾，覽者易知，不重述也。
units.en: What remains scattered through commentaries has mostly been gathered already; the reader can learn it elsewhere, so it is not told again here.
units.literal: The rest scattered in historical notes has largely been gathered; readers may easily know them—not recounted again.

units.zh: 〈諸臺府郎令史職吏以下，具見長水校尉王珪之《職儀》。〉
units.en: 〈For clerks, recorders, and functionaries of the various bureaus and offices, see Colonel of the Long River Wang Guizhi's Protocols of Office.〉
units.literal: 〈Clerks, recorders, and functionaries of the various bureaus and offices are fully set out in Colonel of the Long River Wang Guizhi's "Protocols of Office."〉

units.en: Chancellor of State.
units.literal: Chancellor of State.

units.en: From Xiao He and Cao Shen onward, it was the highest station a subject could hold.
units.literal: Since Xiao He and Cao Shen, it has been the supreme rank for a minister.

units.en: Under Song, Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao held it in the Xiaojian era.
units.literal: In Song's Xiaojian era Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao held it.

units.zh: 至齊不用人，以爲贈，不列官。
units.en: In Qi no living man held it; it was given only as a posthumous honor and dropped from the active roster.
units.literal: By Qi no one was appointed; it served as posthumous grant only and was not listed among active offices.

units.en: Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 宋大明用江夏王義恭，以後無人。
units.en: Song's Prince Yigong of Jiangxia held it in the Daming era; after that, no one.
units.literal: In Song's Daming era Prince Yigong of Jiangxia held it; afterward no one.

units.en: In Qi it was a posthumous title only.
units.literal: Qi used it as posthumous grant.

units.en: Grand Tutor.
units.literal: Grand Tutor.

units.en: Grand Preceptor, Grand Guardian, and Grand Tutor were offices of the Zhou.
units.literal: Grand Preceptor, Grand Guardian, and Grand Tutor were Zhou old offices.

units.en: Late in Han, Dong Zhuo held the Grand Preceptorship.
units.literal: At the end of Han, Dong Zhuo was Grand Preceptor.

units.en: At the start of Jin Huidi's reign, Wei Guan was made Grand Guardian.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jin Emperor Hui's reign, Wei Guan was Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 自後無太師，而太保爲贈。
units.en: Thereafter no one held Grand Preceptor; Grand Guardian survived only as a posthumous grant.
units.literal: Afterward there was no Grand Preceptor, and Grand Guardian became posthumous.

units.en: Qi kept only the Grand Tutor among them.
units.literal: Qi established only the Grand Tutor.

units.en: Grand Marshal.
units.literal: Grand Marshal.

units.en: Grand General.
units.literal: Grand General.

units.zh: 宋元嘉用彭城王義康，後無人。
units.en: In Song's Yuanjia era Prince Yikang of Pengcheng held it; after that, no one.
units.literal: In Song's Yuanjia era Prince Yikang of Pengcheng held it; afterward no one.

units.en: In Qi it was a posthumous title only.
units.literal: Qi used it as posthumous grant.

units.en: Grand Commandant.
units.literal: Grand Commandant.

units.en: Minister of Education.
units.literal: Minister of Education.

units.en: Minister of Works.
units.literal: Minister of Works.

units.en: The Three Excellencies were once standing posts open to appointment.
units.literal: The Three Excellencies were formerly general offices.

units.zh: 司徒府領天下州郡名數戶口簿籍。
units.en: The Minister of Education's bureau kept the empire's registers of place-names, household counts, and population rolls.
units.literal: The Minister of Education's office oversaw registers of household names and population ledgers for all provinces and commanderies under Heaven.

units.zh: 雖無，常置左右長史、左西曹掾屬、主簿、祭酒、令史以下。
units.en: Even when the seat was empty, left and right senior recorders, western-bureau aides, chief clerk, libationer, and recorders below them were always in place.
units.literal: Though vacant, the left and right senior recorders, western-bureau aides-attendant, chief clerk, libationer, and recorders were always installed.

units.zh: 晉世王導爲司徒，右長史干寶撰立官府，《職儀》已具。
units.en: Under Jin, Wang Dao was Minister of Education; his right senior recorder Gan Bao drew up the office establishment—the Protocols of Office already cover it.
units.literal: In Jin times Wang Dao served as Minister of Education; right senior recorder Gan Bao compiled the establishment of the government office—the "Protocols of Office" are complete.

units.en: Special Advance.
units.literal: Special Advance.

units.en: Rank equal to a duke.
units.literal: Rank secondary to the Three Excellencies.

units.en: All holders of Acting Three Excellencies.
units.literal: All Acting Three Excellencies.

units.en: General of Agile Cavalry.
units.literal: General of Agile Cavalry.

units.en: General of Chariots and Cavalry.
units.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry.

units.en: General of the Guard.
units.literal: General of the Guard.

units.en: General Who Guards the Army.
units.literal: General Who Guards the Army.

units.en: General of the Central Army.
units.literal: General of the Central Army.

units.en: General Who Pacifies the Army.
units.literal: General Who Pacifies the Army.

units.en: Four Campaign Generals.
units.literal: Four Campaign Generals.

units.en: 〈East, West, South, North.〉
units.literal: 〈East, West, South, North.〉

units.en: Four Garrison Generals.
units.literal: Four Garrison Generals.

units.zh: 凡諸將軍加「大」字，位從公。
units.en: Any general whose title took the prefix "Grand" ranked equal to a duke.
units.literal: Whenever generals had the character "Great" added, rank equaled a duke.

units.en: An open office with honors equal to the three dukes ranked like a duke.
units.literal: Opened-office honors ranked like a duke.

units.zh: 凡公督府置佐：長史、司馬各一人，諮議參軍二人。
units.en: Every duke-level commandery office appointed aides—one senior recorder and one marshal each, plus two advising staff officers.
units.literal: Every duke's supervisory office set aides: one senior recorder and one marshal each, and two advising staff officers.

units.zh: 諸曹有錄事，功曹，記室，戶曹，倉曹，中、直兵，外兵，騎兵，長流，賊曹，城局，法曹，田曹，水曹，鎧曹，集曹，右戶，十八曹。
units.en: Its bureaus comprised recorders, merit clerks, secretaries, household and granary clerks, central and direct military sections, outer military and cavalry sections, long-service and bandit-suppression sections, city office, law, field, water, armor, assembly, and right-household sections—eighteen bureaus in all.
units.literal: The bureaus had recorders, merit clerks, secretaries, household clerks, granary clerks, central and direct military clerks, outer military clerks, cavalry clerks, long-service clerks, bandit-suppression clerks, city-office clerks, law clerks, field clerks, water clerks, armor clerks, assembly clerks, and right-household clerks—eighteen bureaus.

units.zh: 城局曹以上署正參軍，法曹以下署行參軍，各一人。
units.en: From the city-office bureau up, each post had a regular staff officer; from the law bureau down, an acting staff officer.
units.literal: From the city-office bureau upward one regular staff officer was posted; from the law bureau downward one acting staff officer each.

units.zh: 其行參軍無署者，爲長兼員。
units.en: An acting staff officer without a dedicated post served as a standing concurrent appointee.
units.literal: Where an acting staff officer had no post, he served as long-term concurrent member.

units.zh: 其府佐史則從事中郎二人，倉曹掾、戶曹屬、東西閤祭酒各一人，主簿舍人御屬二人。
units.en: Office aides and clerks comprised two attendant gentlemen, a granary aide, a household subordinate, eastern and western pavilion libationers, and two chief-clerk secretaries with imperial attendants.
units.literal: The office aides and clerks were two attendant gentlemen, one granary bureau aide, one household bureau subordinate, one libationer each for the eastern and western pavilions, and two chief-clerk secretaries and imperial attendants.

units.zh: 加崇者，則左右長史四人，中郎掾屬竝增數。
units.en: With added honors came four senior recorders, left and right, and more attendant gentlemen and subordinates.
units.literal: When honors were raised, there were four left and right senior recorders, and the attendant gentlemen and subordinates were increased in number.

units.zh: 其未及開府，則置府亦有佐史，其數有減。
units.en: Even without an open office, a commandery staff kept aides and clerks—though fewer.
units.literal: Those not yet granted an open office still had office aides and clerks, but in reduced numbers.

units.zh: 小府無長流，置禁防參軍。
units.en: Small staffs omitted the long-service bureau and posted a garrison-defense staff officer instead.
units.literal: Small offices had no long-service bureau; they posted a garrison-defense staff officer.

units.en: Four Pacification Generals.
units.literal: Four Pacification Generals.

units.en: Four Tranquility Generals.
units.literal: Four Tranquility Generals.

units.en: Generals of the Left, Right, Front, and Rear.
units.literal: Generals of the Left, Right, Front, and Rear.

units.en: General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
units.literal: General Who Subdues the Barbarians.

units.en: Four Central Guard Commandants.
units.literal: Four Central Guard Commandants.

units.zh: 晉世荀羨、王胡之竝居此官。
units.en: Under Jin, Xun Xian and Wang Huzhi both held the post.
units.literal: In Jin times Xun Xian and Wang Huzhi both held this office.

units.zh: 宋、齊以來，唯處諸王，素族無爲者。
units.en: From Song and Qi onward it went only to imperial princes; no commoner clan ever held it.
units.literal: Since Song and Qi, only imperial princes received it; no common clan ever did.

units.en: General Who Champions.
units.literal: General Who Champions.

units.en: General Who Assists the State.
units.literal: General Who Assists the State.

units.en: General Who Pacifies the North.
units.literal: General Who Pacifies the North.

units.en: General Who Pacifies the Distance.
units.literal: General Who Pacifies the Distance.

units.en: Dragon-Courser General.
units.literal: Dragon-Courser General.

units.en: Even some of these lesser titles could open a full staff office.
units.literal: Among these lesser titles, some also had offices established.

units.en: Minister of Ceremonies.
units.literal: Minister of Ceremonies.

units.zh: 府置丞一人，五官、功曹、主簿，九府九史皆然。
units.en: Its office had one deputy, five officers, a merit clerk, and a chief clerk—the same pattern as the other eight ministries and their clerks.
units.literal: The office had one deputy, plus five officers, merit clerk, and chief clerk—the nine ministries and nine clerks were all alike.

units.en: It oversaw the following posts:
units.literal: Subordinate offices are as follows:

units.en: Erudites, styled erudites of the Grand Academy.
units.literal: Erudites—called erudites of the Grand Academy.

units.en: One director of the Imperial Academy.
units.literal: One director of the Imperial Academy.

units.en: Two erudites.
units.literal: Two erudites.

units.en: Ten teaching assistants.
units.literal: Ten teaching assistants.

units.zh: 建元四年，有司奏置國學，祭酒准諸曹尚書，博士准中書郎，助教准南臺御史。
units.en: In the fourth year of Jianyuan the ministries proposed a national academy: its director ranked with a bureau director of the masters of writing, its erudites with a secretariat gentleman, its assistants with a Southern Bureau censor.
units.literal: In Jianyuan year 4 the relevant offices memorialized to establish the national academy: the director's rank equaled directors of the masters of writing in other bureaus, erudites equaled secretariat gentlemen, and assistants equaled censors of the Southern Bureau.

units.en: Candidates were chosen first for mastery of the classics.
units.literal: Classical learning came first in selection.

units.zh: 若其人難備，給事中以還明經者，以本位領。
units.en: When no one qualified could be found, a palace attendant who had passed the classics examination might serve concurrently in his present rank.
units.literal: If suitable men were hard to find, a palace attendant who had passed the classics examination might lead in his existing post.

units.zh: 其下典學二人，三品，准太常主簿；
units.en: Below them stood two academy directors of third rank, equal to the Minister of Ceremonies' chief clerk;
units.literal: Below them were two academy directors, third rank, equivalent to the Minister of Ceremonies' chief clerk;

units.en: two household clerks and two ritual clerks each, fifth rank;
units.literal: two household clerks and two ritual clerks each, fifth rank;

units.en: eight white-register clerks for ritual paperwork, sixth rank;
units.literal: eight white-register clerks for ritual administration, sixth rank;

units.en: two academy physicians;
units.literal: two academy physicians;

units.en: two masters of ceremony.
units.literal: two masters of ceremony.

units.zh: 其夏，國諱廢學，有司奏省助教以下。
units.en: That summer mourning for the late emperor closed the schools; the ministries proposed cutting every post below teaching assistant.
units.literal: That summer, because of the imperial mourning taboo the schools were suspended; the ministries memorialized to abolish posts below teaching assistant.

units.zh: 永明三年，立學，尚書令王儉領祭酒。
units.en: In Yongming 3 the academy was restored; Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian served as its director.
units.literal: In Yongming year 3 the academy was re-established; Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian headed it as director.

units.zh: 八年，國子博士何胤單爲祭酒，疑所服，陸澄等皆不能據，遂以玄服臨試。
units.en: In year 8 the academy erudite He Yin became sole director; with no precedent for his robes, Lu Cheng and the rest could not decide, and he examined candidates in black dress.
units.literal: In year 8 the academy erudite He Yin alone became director; uncertain what robes to wear, Lu Cheng and others could cite no precedent, so he presided over examinations in black garb.

units.zh: 月餘日，博議定，乃服朱衣。
units.en: After a month of debate among scholars, he took vermilion robes.
units.literal: After a month and more of broad deliberation, he donned vermilion robes.

units.en: One director of the Zongming Observatory.
units.literal: One director of the Zongming Observatory.

units.zh: 右太始六年，以國學廢，初置總明觀，玄、儒、文、史四科，科置學士各十人，正令史一人，書令史二人，幹一人，門吏一人，典觀吏二人。
units.en: Note: In the sixth year of Taishi, with the national academy shut, the Zongming Observatory was founded—Daoist, Confucian, literary, and historical sections, ten scholars each; plus one chief recorder, two document recorders, a steward, a gate officer, and two observatory clerks.
units.literal: Note: In Taishi year 6, when the national academy was abolished, the Zongming Observatory was first established—four disciplines, Daoist, Confucian, literary, and historical, each with ten scholars; one chief recorder, two document recorders, one steward, one gate officer, and two observatory clerks.

units.en: In the Jianyuan era it managed the five rites.
units.literal: During Jianyuan it oversaw the five rites.

units.en: When the national academy reopened in Yongming 3, the observatory was abolished.
units.literal: In Yongming year 3 the national academy was built, and it was abolished.

units.en: Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, one; deputy, one.
units.literal: Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, one; deputy, one.

units.en: Director of the Bright Hall, one; deputy, one.
units.literal: Director of the Bright Hall, one; deputy, one.

units.en: Director of Imperial Sacrifices, one; deputy, one.
units.literal: Director of Imperial Sacrifices, one; deputy, one.

units.en: Director of the Imperial Astronomer, one; deputy, one.
units.literal: Director of the Imperial Astronomer, one; deputy, one.

units.en: Director of Sacrificial Victims: one; aide: one.
units.literal: Director of Sacrificial Victims: one; aide: one.

units.en: Below the director and aide, functional clerks were all appointed.
units.literal: Below the director and aide, all had functional clerks appointed.

units.en: Grand Musician: one; aide: one.
units.literal: Grand Musician: one; aide: one.

units.en: Directors of the imperial tombs.
units.literal: Directors of the imperial tombs.

units.zh: 永明末置，用二品三品勳。
units.en: Established at the end of Yongming; appointees were drawn from holders of second- and third-rank merit.
units.literal: Established at the end of Yongming; men of second- and third-rank merit were used.

units.zh: 置主簿、戶曹各一人，六品保舉。
units.en: One registrar and one household-section chief were appointed; candidates were nominated at rank six.
units.literal: One registrar and one household-section chief were appointed; selections were nominated at rank six.

units.en: Supervisor of Attendants.
units.literal: Supervisor of Attendants.

units.en: The bureau had one aide.
units.literal: The bureau had one aide.

units.en: It oversaw the following posts:
units.literal: Subordinate offices are as follows:

units.en: Left and Right Grandees of Splendor.
units.literal: Left and Right Grandees of Splendor.

units.zh: 位從公，開府置佐史如公。
units.en: Rank equivalent to a duke; they opened a bureau and appointed aides and clerks like a duke.
units.literal: Rank equivalent to a duke; they opened a bureau and appointed aides and clerks as for a duke.

units.en: Grandee of Splendor.
units.literal: Grandee of Splendor.

units.zh: 皆銀章青綬，詔加金章紫綬者，爲金紫光祿大夫。
units.en: All bore silver seals and green ribbons; when an edict added a golden seal and purple ribbon, the holder became a Grandee of Splendor with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
units.literal: All had silver seals and green ribbons; those whom an edict added a golden seal and purple ribbon became Grandees of Splendor with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

units.zh: 樂安任遐爲光祿，就王晏乞一片金，晏乃啓轉爲金紫，不行。
units.en: Ren Xia of Le'an held the grandeeship of splendor; he asked Wang Yan for a piece of gold, and Yan memorialized to promote him to golden seal and purple ribbon, but the request failed.
units.literal: Ren Xia of Le'an was grandee of splendor; he asked Wang Yan for a piece of gold, and Yan memorialized to transfer him to golden seal and purple ribbon, but it did not go through.

units.en: Superior Grandee of the Palace.
units.literal: Superior Grandee of the Palace.

units.en: Palace Attendant Grandee.
units.literal: Palace Attendant Grandee.

units.zh: 諸大夫官，皆處舊齒老年，重者加親信二十人。
units.en: These grand-master posts went to men of long service and advanced years; for the more honored posts, twenty personal attendants were added.
units.literal: For all these grand-master posts, men of old standing and advanced years were placed; for the weightier posts, twenty personal attendants were added.

units.en: Commandant of the Guards.
units.literal: Commandant of the Guards.

units.en: The bureau had one aide.
units.literal: The bureau had one aide.

units.en: He oversaw the palace city's gates and keys.
units.literal: He oversaw the palace city's gates and keys.

units.zh: 張衡西京賦曰「衞尉八屯，警夜巡晝」。
units.en: Zhang Heng's Western Capital Rhapsody says, "The commandant of the guards' eight garrisons—alert at night, patrol by day."
units.literal: Zhang Heng's Western Capital Rhapsody says, "The Commandant of the Guards' eight garrisons—alert at night, patrol by day."

units.zh: 宮城諸却敵樓上本施鼓，持夜者以應更唱，太祖以鼓多驚眠，改以鐵磬云。
units.en: On every parapet tower of the palace city drums had once been set up, and night watchmen answered the watch-change call with them. The Founder, saying the drums too often broke sleep, is said to have replaced them with iron chimes.
units.literal: On all the parapet towers of the palace city drums had originally been installed; night watchmen answered the change of watch by drumming. The Founder, finding the drums often startled sleep, changed them to iron chimes, it is said.

units.en: Commandant of Justice.
units.literal: Commandant of Justice.

units.zh: 府置丞一人，正一人，監一人，評一人，律博士一人。
units.en: The bureau had one aide, one chief judge, one inspector, one reviewer, and one doctor of law.
units.literal: The bureau had one aide, one chief judge, one inspector, one reviewer, and one doctor of law.

units.en: Grand Minister of Agriculture.
units.literal: Grand Minister of Agriculture.

units.literal: The bureau had one aide.

units.literal: Director of the Grand Granary: one; aide: one.

units.literal: Left and Right Directors of the Imperial Workshops: one each; aide: one each.

units.literal: 〈Removed in Yongming 3, restored in 4.〉

units.literal: Director of the Imperial Wardrobe: one; aide: one.

units.literal: The Master of Works oversaw palace and temple construction in earth and wood.

units.literal: The Director of the Imperial Stud oversaw suburban rites and held the reins.

units.en: The Grand Herald oversaw escort, presentation, and praise at audience.
units.literal: The Grand Herald oversaw escort, presentation, and praise at audience.

units.en: When need arose, concurrent posts were set up ad hoc; when the task ended, they were abolished.
units.literal: When there was business, concurrent posts were set up ad hoc; when finished, they were abolished.

units.en: Director of the Chariots and Horses, one person.
units.literal: Director of the Chariots and Horses, one person.

units.zh: 掌五輅安車，大行凶器轀輬車。
units.en: He managed the five regalia chariots, the comfort carriage, and the great-procession funeral wagons and bier-carriages.
units.literal: In charge of the five regalia chariots and the comfort carriage, and of the great-procession funeral wagons and bier-carriages.

units.en: Director of the Guest Lodge.
units.literal: Director of the Guest Lodge.

units.en: He received guests from all four quarters.
units.literal: In charge of guests from all four quarters.

units.en: Xuande Minister of the Guard, Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues, and Chamberlain for the Imperial Stud.
units.literal: Xuande Minister of the Guard, Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues, and Chamberlain for the Imperial Stud.

units.zh: 鬱林王立，文安太后卽尊號，以宮名置之。
units.en: When the Prince of Yulin was enthroned and Empress Dowager Wen'an took her honorific title, these offices were created and named after palace quarters.
units.literal: When the Prince of Yulin was made heir, Empress Dowager Wen'an assumed her honorific title, and these posts were established bearing palace names.

units.en: Grand Chamberlain for the Palace Environs.
units.literal: Grand Chamberlain for the Palace Environs.

units.en: Established when the Prince of Yulin raised his consort to empress.
units.literal: Established when the Prince of Yulin made his consort empress.

units.en: Recorder of the masters of writing.
units.literal: Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

units.en: Director of the masters of writing.
units.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 總領尚書臺二十曹，爲內臺主。
units.en: He headed all twenty departments of the secretariat and served as chief of the inner office.
units.literal: He oversaw all twenty departments of the Masters-of-Writing Secretariat and was chief of the inner office.

units.en: On the road, everyone from princes down had to stop and make way.
units.literal: When he traveled on the road, everyone from princes downward had to halt.

units.en: The left and right vice directors used separate routes.
units.literal: The left and right vice directors traveled by separate routes.

units.zh: 無令，左僕射爲臺主，與令同。
units.en: If the directorate was vacant, the left vice director headed the secretariat with the director's authority.
units.literal: When there was no director, the left vice director was head of the secretariat, with the same authority as the director.

units.en: Left vice director.
units.literal: Left Vice Director.

units.zh: 領殿中主客二曹事，諸曹郊廟、園陵、車駕行幸、朝儀、臺內非違、文官舉補滿敘疾假事，其諸吉慶瑞應衆賀、災異賊發衆變、臨軒崇拜、改號格制、莅官銓選，凡諸除署、功論、封爵、貶黜、八議、疑讞、通關案，則左僕射主，右僕射次經，維是黃案，左僕射右僕射署朱符見字，經都丞竟，右僕射橫畫成目，左僕射畫，令畫。
units.en: He oversaw the Palace and Guest-Relations bureaus. Across the departments he took the lead on suburban and temple rites, imperial tombs, progresses, court ceremony, internal discipline, civil appointments and promotions, completed terms, and sick leave; on congratulatory rites for good omens, mass celebrations, disasters, rebellions, and other emergencies; on imperial-audience worship, era-title and regulatory changes, and arrival and selection of officials; and on every appointment, merit review, enfeoffment, demotion, eight deliberations, doubtful case, and transit permit—the left vice director led and the right vice director followed. On yellow documents both vice directors applied red seals and visible endorsements; after the secretariat aide finished review, the right vice director drew a horizontal closing stroke, then the left vice director and the director signed.
units.literal: He oversaw the Palace and Guest-Relations departments. For all departments—suburban and temple sacrifices, imperial tombs, imperial progresses, court ritual, internal secretariat violations, civil appointments, promotions, completed tenure, and sick leave; and for all congratulatory rites for auspicious omens, mass felicitations, disasters, bandit outbreaks, and collective emergencies, imperial-audience worship, changes of era titles and regulations, arrival at post and selection of officers, and every appointment, merit evaluation, enfeoffment, demotion, eight deliberations, doubtful cases, and transit permits—the left vice director took primary responsibility and the right vice director handled secondary routing. For yellow documents, the left and right vice directors affixed red seals and visible endorsements; after the secretariat aide completed review, the right vice director drew a horizontal stroke to close the entry, the left vice director signed, and the director signed.

units.en: If the official on the right was absent, the next in line signed together.
units.literal: If the right-hand official was absent, the next in order signed jointly.

units.zh: 若無左右，則直置僕射在其中閒，總左右事。
units.en: If neither left nor right vice director was in place, one vice director was appointed between them to handle both sides.
units.literal: If there were neither left nor right, a single vice director was placed between them to oversee both sides' duties.

units.en: Minister of the ministry of personnel.
units.literal: Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

units.zh: 領吏部、刪定、三公、比部四曹。
units.en: He oversaw the Personnel, Revision, Three Excellencies, and Comparison bureaus.
units.literal: He oversaw the Personnel, Revision, Three Excellencies, and Comparison departments.

units.en: Minister of revenue.
units.literal: Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 領度支、金部、倉部、起部四曹。
units.en: He oversaw the Revenue, Gold, Granary, and Construction bureaus.
units.literal: He oversaw the Revenue, Gold, Granary, and Construction departments.

units.en: Minister for the left populace.
units.literal: Minister for the Left Populace.

units.en: He oversaw the Left Populace and Chariot bureaus.
units.literal: He oversaw the Left Populace and Chariot departments.

units.en: Minister of justice.
units.literal: Minister of Justice.

units.zh: 領都官、水部、庫部、功論四曹。
units.en: He oversaw the Justice, Water, Stores, and Merit-Evaluation bureaus.
units.literal: He oversaw the Justice, Water, Stores, and Merit-Evaluation departments.

units.en: Minister of the five armies.
units.literal: Minister of the Five Armies.

units.en: He oversaw the Inner and Outer Military bureaus.
units.literal: He oversaw the Inner and Outer Military departments.

units.en: Minister of the sacrificial department.
units.literal: Minister of the Sacrificial Department.

units.en: The right vice director held the post concurrently, and the two were not appointed separately.
units.literal: The right vice director held it concurrently, and both were not separately appointed.

units.en: Minister of construction.
units.literal: Minister of Construction.

units.en: Created temporarily to erect palaces and temples, then abolished when the work ended.
units.literal: Temporarily established for building palaces and temples; abolished when the work was finished.

units.en: Left aide, one person.
units.literal: Left aide, one person.

units.zh: 掌宗廟郊祠、吉慶瑞應、災異、立作格制、諸案彈、選用除置、吏補滿除遣注職。
units.en: He handled suburban and temple sacrifices, auspicious omens and congratulatory rites, disasters and anomalies, new regulations, case reviews and impeachments, appointments and dismissals, filling vacancies, and posting officials to duty.
units.literal: He handled suburban and temple sacrifices, auspicious omens and congratulatory rites, disasters and anomalies, new regulations, case reviews and impeachments, appointments and dismissals, filling vacancies, and assigning posts.

units.en: Right aide, one person.
units.literal: Right aide, one person.

units.zh: 掌兵士百工補役死叛考代年老疾病解遣、其內外諸庫藏穀帛、刑辠創業諍訟、田地船乘、稟拘兵工死叛、考剔討補、差分百役、兵器諸營署人領、州郡租布、民戶移徙、州郡縣併帖、城邑民戶割屬、刺史二千石令長丞尉被收及免贈、文武諸犯削官事。
units.en: He handled soldiers and artisans—recruitment, replacements for the dead and deserters, evaluations, and release for age, sickness, or disability; grain and silk in state storehouses inside and out; criminal, property, and litigation matters; land, boats, and transport; laborers who died or fled service, review, replacement, and corvée assignment; arms, camps, and workshop staffing; provincial and commandery cloth taxes; household moves; mergers of provinces, commanderies, and counties; reassignment of city populations; arrest, removal, reward, or posthumous honors for inspectors, two-thousand-shi officials, and county magistrates, aides, and commandants; and every civil or military case that stripped an office.
units.literal: He handled soldiers and artisans—recruitment, replacements for death and desertion, evaluations, release for age, illness, or disability; all internal and external granaries and treasuries of grain and silk; criminal cases, land disputes, and lawsuits; fields, boats, and transport; conscription of laborers who died or deserted, assessments, replacements, and allocation of corvée; arms, garrison personnel, and workshop staffing; provincial and commandery tax deliveries in cloth; household migration; mergers of provinces, commanderies, and counties; reassignment of urban households; arrest, dismissal, reward, or posthumous honors for inspectors, two-thousand-shi officials, magistrates, aides, and commandants; and all civil and military cases involving stripping of office.

units.zh: 白案，右丞上署，左丞次署。
units.en: On white documents the right aide signed first and the left aide second.
units.literal: For white documents, the right aide signed first and the left aide second.

units.zh: 黃案，左丞上署，右丞次署。
units.en: On yellow documents the left aide signed first and the right aide second.
units.literal: For yellow documents, the left aide signed first and the right aide second.

units.zh: 諸立格制及詳讞大事宗廟朝廷儀體，左丞上署，右丞次署。
units.en: For new regulations and major reviewed cases on ancestral temples and court ritual, the left aide signed first and the right aide second.
units.literal: For all new regulations and major reviewed cases concerning ancestral temples and court ceremonial, the left aide signed first and the right aide second.

units.zh: 自令僕以下五尚書八座二十曹，各置郎中令史以下，又置都令史分領之。
units.en: From the director and vice directors through the five ministers, eight seats, and twenty bureaus, each office had gentlemen-attendants and clerks below them, with chief clerks assigned to supervise.
units.literal: From the director and vice directors down through the five ministers, eight seats, and twenty departments, each had gentleman-attendants and clerks; chief clerks were also appointed to oversee them.

units.zh: 僕射掌朝軌，尚書掌讞奏，都丞任碎，在彈違諸曹緣常及外詳讞事。
units.en: Vice directors managed court protocol, directors handled memorials, and secretariat aides handled detail—checking routine violations in the bureaus and reviewing outside cases.
units.literal: The vice directors managed court protocol; the directors handled memorials; the secretariat aides handled detail, rebuking violations in routine department matters and external case review.

units.zh: 應須命議相值者，皆郎先立意，應奏黃案及關事，以立意官爲議主。
units.en: When consultation was needed, gentlemen-attendants drafted the proposal first; for yellow-document memorials and related business, the drafter chaired the discussion.
units.literal: When deliberation was required, gentlemen-attendants first drafted the position; for yellow-document memorials and related matters, the drafting officer chaired discussion.

units.zh: 凡辭訴有漫命者，曹緣諮如舊。
units.en: Petitions with vague instructions were routed through the bureaus as before.
units.literal: For all petitions lacking clear orders, departments consulted as before.

units.zh: 若命有諮，則以立意者爲議主。
units.en: If the order called for consultation, the drafter chaired the discussion.
units.literal: If the order required consultation, the drafting officer chaired discussion.

units.en: Director of the arsenal, one person.
units.literal: Director of the Arsenal, one person.

units.en: Subordinate to the Stores bureau.
units.literal: Subordinate to the Stores department.

units.en: Director of the carriage office, one person; aide, one person.
units.literal: Director of the Carriage Office, one person; aide, one person.

units.en: Subordinate to the Chariot bureau.
units.literal: Subordinate to the Chariot department.

units.en: Director of the imperial carriages, one person.
units.literal: Director of the Imperial Carriages, one person.

units.en: Director of the commissariat, one person; aide, one person.
units.literal: Director of the Commissariat, one person; aide, one person.

units.en: Grand Physician-in-Chief, one person; aide, one person.
units.literal: Grand Physician-in-Chief, one person; aide, one person.

units.en: Inner and outer superintendents of the palace halls, one each.
units.literal: Inner and outer Superintendents of the Palace Halls, one each.

units.en: Inner and outer assistant directors of the piebald stud, one each.
units.literal: Inner and outer assistant directors of the Piebald Stud, one each.

units.zh: 材官將軍一人，司馬一人。
units.en: General of materiel, one person; marshal, one person.
units.literal: General of Materiel, one person; marshal, one person.

units.en: He answered to the Construction Department and also to the Army Lead Office.
units.literal: Subordinate to the Construction Department; also subordinate to the Army Lead Office.

units.en: Chief of the gentlemen-in-attendance of the palace gate.
units.literal: Chief of the Gentlemen-in-Attendance of the Palace Gate.

units.en: 〈So titled for those of highest merit.〉
units.literal: 〈So titled for those of highest merit.〉

units.en: Gentlemen-in-attendance of the palace gate.
units.literal: Gentlemen-in-Attendance of the Palace Gate.

units.en: Under the Han it was a post kept close to the throne.
units.literal: In Han times it was an intimate post at court.

units.zh: 魏、晉選用，稍增華重，而大意不異。
units.en: Wei and Jin made the appointment somewhat grander, yet its heart stayed the same.
units.literal: Under Wei and Jin selection it gained a little more splendor and weight, but the essential character did not change.

units.zh: 宋文帝元嘉中，王華、王曇首、殷景仁等，竝爲侍中，情在親密，與帝接膝共語，貂拂帝手，拔貂置案上，語畢復手插之。
units.en: In Emperor Wen of Song's Yuanjia years Wang Hua, Wang Tan-shou, Yin Jingren, and others served together as gentlemen-in-attendance, intimate enough to talk knee to knee with the emperor—brushing his hand with their sable, slipping it off to lay on the table, then, when words were spent, sliding their hands back in.
units.literal: In the Yuanjia era of Emperor Wen of Song, Wang Hua, Wang Tan-shou, Yin Jingren, and others all served as gentlemen-in-attendance; close in feeling, they spoke with the emperor knee to knee, brushed the imperial hand with their sable, drew the sable off and laid it on the table, and when speech was done slipped their hands back in.

units.zh: 孝武時，侍中何偃南郊陪乘，鑾輅過白門閫，偃將匐，帝乃接之曰：「朕乃陪卿。」
units.en: Under Emperor Xiaowu, He Yan, gentleman-in-attendance, rode beside the emperor at the southern suburb; as the train passed the White Gate barbican he was about to bow flat, and the emperor stayed him: "I shall keep you company."
units.literal: In the Xiaowu era the gentleman-in-attendance He Yan rode beside the emperor at the southern suburb; when the imperial carriage passed the White Gate barbican Yan was about to prostrate himself, and the emperor caught him up, saying, "I shall accompany you."

units.zh: 齊世朝會，多以美姿容者兼官。
units.en: In Qi, court levees often doubled handsome men in other offices.
units.literal: In Qi, court assemblies often gave concurrent posts to men of handsome bearing.

units.zh: 永元三年，東昏南郊，不欲親朝士，以主璽陪乘，前代未嘗有也。
units.en: In Yongyuan's third year Emperor Donghun, going to the southern suburb, refused to face the court gentlemen and set the keeper of the imperial seal beside him in the carriage—a thing no age before had seen.
units.literal: In the third year of Yongyuan, when Emperor Donghun went to the southern suburb he would not face the court gentlemen and had the Keeper of the Imperial Seal ride beside him—something no earlier age had done.

units.en: In court speech they were called "Gate Below."
units.literal: The gentlemen-in-attendance were called "Gate Below."

units.en: Clerk-recorders were appointed as well.
units.literal: Clerk-recorders were also appointed.

units.en: It oversaw the following posts:
units.literal: Subordinate offices are as follows:

units.en: Gentlemen attendants of the yellow gate.
units.literal: Gentlemen Attendants of the Yellow Gate.

units.zh: 亦管知詔令，世呼爲小門下。
units.en: They also handled edicts and orders; courtiers called them "Lesser Gate Below."
units.literal: Also in charge of edicts and orders; in common speech, "Lesser Gate Below."

units.en: Regular attendant-in-ordinary.
units.literal: Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.en: Direct regular attendant-in-ordinary.
units.literal: Direct Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.en: Supernumerary regular attendant-in-ordinary.
units.literal: Supernumerary Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.zh: 舊與侍中通官，其通直員外，用衰老人士，故其官漸替。
units.en: Once they had shared rank with the gentlemen-in-attendance; direct and supernumerary posts went to aged men of note, and the office slowly hollowed out.
units.literal: Formerly they shared office with the gentlemen-in-attendance; the direct and supernumerary posts were given to elderly men of standing, so the rank gradually declined.

units.zh: 宋大明雖華選比侍中，而人情久習，終不見重，尋復如初。
units.en: In Song's Daming years the post was chosen with as much show as the gentlemen-in-attendance, yet custom had taught men not to esteem it, and soon it sank back to the old level.
units.literal: In the Daming era of Song the selection was as splendid as for gentlemen-in-attendance, but long habit kept it from winning regard, and before long it returned to what it had been.

units.en: Gentleman cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
units.literal: Gentleman Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.en: Direct gentleman cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
units.literal: Direct Gentleman Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.en: Supernumerary gentleman cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
units.literal: Supernumerary Gentleman Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.en: Gentlemen for palace service.
units.literal: Gentlemen for Palace Service.

units.en: Court attendants at imperial audience.
units.literal: Court Attendants at Imperial Audience.

units.en: Commandant of the horse-consorts.
units.literal: Commandant of the Horse-Consorts.

units.en: Duties of the Secretariat for Imperial Writings; chief clerks for documents were posted.
units.literal: Duties of the Secretariat for Imperial Writings; chief clerks for documents were appointed.

units.zh: 朝散用衣冠之餘，人數猥積。
units.en: Court attendants at audience were filled from men who had left the cap and gown; the rolls swelled past counting.
units.literal: Court attendants at audience were drawn from the leavings of formal office; their numbers piled up without measure.

units.zh: 永明中，奉朝請至六百餘人。
units.en: By the Yongming years court attendants at audience numbered more than six hundred.
units.literal: In the Yongming era there were more than six hundred court attendants at audience.

units.zh: 中書監一人，令一人，侍郎四人，通事舍人無員。
units.en: Superintendent of the palace secretariat, one; director, one; four gentlemen-attendants; palace messengers without fixed quota.
units.literal: Superintendent of the Palace Secretariat, one person; director, one person; four gentlemen-attendants; palace messengers without fixed quota.

units.zh: 中書省職，置主書、令史、正書以下。
units.en: Duties of the palace secretariat; chief document clerks, recorder-clerks, document officers, and ranks below were posted.
units.literal: Duties of the Palace Secretariat; chief document clerks, clerk-recorders, document officers, and below were appointed.

units.en: Director of the imperial library, one person; aide, one person.
units.literal: Director of the Imperial Library, one person; aide, one person.

units.en: Gentleman.
units.literal: Gentleman.

units.en: Assistant gentleman for compilation.
units.literal: Assistant Gentleman for Compilation.

units.zh: 晉祕書閣有令史，掌衆書，見《晉令》，令亦置令史、正書及弟子，皆典教書畫。
units.en: Under Jin the library pavilion kept clerk-recorders over all books, per the Jin statutes; the director likewise posted clerk-recorders, document officers, and disciples, all to teach writing and painting.
units.literal: Under Jin the library pavilion had clerk-recorders in charge of all books, as in the Jin statutes; the director also appointed clerk-recorders, document officers, and disciples, all charged with teaching writing and painting.

units.en: Inspector-in-chief of the censorate, one person.
units.literal: Inspector-in-Chief of the Censorate, one person.

units.zh: 晉江左中丞司隷分督百僚，傅咸所云「行馬內外」是也。
units.en: East of the Yangzi under Jin the inspector-in-chief and the capital director split supervision of the hundred officials—Fu Xian's "running horses inside and out."
units.literal: Under Jin east of the Yangzi the inspector-in-chief and the director of the capital shared oversight of the hundred officials—what Fu Xian called "running horses inside and out."

units.zh: 今中丞則職無不察，專道而行，騶輻禁呵，加以聲色，武將相逢，輙致侵犯，若有鹵簿，至相敺擊。
units.en: Now the inspector-in-chief looks into everything; he keeps his own road, outriders and guards shouting the way clear, pomp and voice together. Military men who meet him often clash; where an imperial train passes, blows may be exchanged.
units.literal: Today the inspector-in-chief has no matter he does not examine; he travels in his own lane, with outriders and guards shouting him clear, voice and display together; when he meets military officers they often trespass, and if there is an imperial train they may come to blows.

units.zh: 宋孝建二年制，中丞與尚書令分道，雖丞郎下朝相值，亦得斷之，餘內外衆官，皆受停駐。
units.en: Song's Xiaojian second year fixed that the inspector-in-chief and the director of the masters of writing took different roads; even aides and gentlemen meeting him after court could be stopped, and every other officer within or without had to pull aside.
units.literal: A regulation of the second year of Xiaojian in Song: the inspector-in-chief and the director of the masters of writing used separate routes; even when aides and gentlemen met him leaving court they might halt him, and all other officials inside and out had to stop.

units.en: Gentlemen for legal documents, two persons.
units.literal: Gentlemen for Legal Documents, two persons.

units.en: Gentlemen attendants of the censorate, ten persons.
units.literal: Gentlemen Attendants of the Censorate, ten persons.

units.zh: 蘭臺置諸曹內外督令以下。
units.en: The Orchid Terrace posted internal and external overseers, commanders, and ranks below for the various bureaus.
units.literal: The Orchid Terrace set up the various bureaus' internal and external overseers, commanders, and below.

units.en: Superintendent of the receptionists, one person.
units.literal: Superintendent of the Receptionists, one person.

units.en: Receptionists, ten persons.
units.literal: Receptionists, ten persons.

units.en: The Receptionists' Office handled court audiences and banquets for guests.
units.literal: The Receptionists' Office managed court audiences and guest banquets.

units.en: General Who Leads the Army; General of the Central Army Who Leads the Army.
units.literal: General Who Leads the Army; General of the Central Army Who Leads the Army.

units.en: General Who Protects the Army; General of the Central Army Who Protects the Army.
units.literal: General Who Protects the Army; General of the Central Army Who Protects the Army.

units.en: Posts marked central, minor, or light were the same office.
units.literal: Any post with zhong, xiao, or qing is the same office.

units.en: Every general had to show deference to the Army Lead and Protect generals.
units.literal: All who held general posts showed respect to the Army Lead and Protect generals.

units.zh: 諸王爲將軍，道相逢，則領、護讓道。
units.en: If a prince holding a generalship met them on the road, the Army Lead and Protect generals gave way.
units.literal: When princes who were generals met on the road, the Army Lead and Protect generals yielded the road.

units.zh: 置長史、司馬、五官、功曹、主簿。
units.en: Each office had a senior recorder, marshal, five officers, merit clerk, and registrar.
units.literal: They appointed a senior recorder, marshal, five officers, merit clerk, and registrar.

units.en: Left and right guard generals.
units.literal: Left and Right Guard Generals.

units.en: Valiant Cavalry General.
units.literal: Valiant Cavalry General.

units.en: Roving General.
units.literal: Roving General.

units.zh: 晉世以來，謂領、護至驍、游爲六軍。
units.en: Since Jin, the Army Lead and Protect posts through Valiant Cavalry and Roving were known as the Six Armies.
units.literal: From Jin times onward, Army Lead and Protect through Valiant Cavalry and Roving were called the Six Armies.

units.zh: 二衞置司馬次官功曹主簿以下。
units.en: The two guard offices appointed marshals, deputy staff officers, merit clerks, and registrars and below.
units.literal: The two guards offices had marshals, deputy staff officers, merit clerks, and registrars and below.

units.en: Left and right central gentlemen of the suite.
units.literal: Left and Right Central Gentlemen of the Suite.

units.zh: 前軍將軍、後軍將軍、左軍將軍、右軍將軍，號四軍。
units.en: Front, rear, left, and right army generals—called the Four Armies.
units.literal: Front Army General, Rear Army General, Left Army General, and Right Army General—called the Four Armies.

units.zh: 屯騎、步兵、射聲、越騎、長水五校尉。
units.en: Commandants of escort cavalry, footsoldiers, volley sound, crossbow cavalry, and long water—the five commandants.
units.literal: Commandants of Escort Cavalry, Footsoldiers, Volley Sound, Crossbow Cavalry, and Long Water—the five commandants.

units.en: Captain of the Rapid Tiger Guard in the suite of attendants.
units.literal: Captain of the Rapid Tiger Guard in the Suite of Attendants.

units.en: Master of retainers on extraordinary assignment.
units.literal: Master of Retainers on Extraordinary Assignment.

units.en: Superintendent of the Feathered Forest.
units.literal: Superintendent of the Feathered Forest.

units.en: General of Accumulated Volleys.
units.literal: General of Accumulated Volleys.

units.en: Strong Crossbow General.
units.literal: Strong Crossbow General.

units.zh: 殿中將軍、員外殿中將軍。
units.en: Palace-hall general; supernumerary palace-hall general.
units.literal: Palace-Hall General; supernumerary Palace-Hall General.

units.en: Director of palace-hall staff officers.
units.literal: Director of Palace-Hall Staff Officers.

units.en: Martial Guard General.
units.literal: Martial Guard General.

units.en: Martial cavalry attendant-in-ordinary.
units.literal: Martial Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.zh: 自二衞、四軍、五校已下，謂之「西省」，而散騎爲「東省」。
units.en: From the two guards, four armies, and five commandants down was the "Western Bureau"; attendant cavalier posts formed the "Eastern Bureau."
units.literal: From the two guards, four armies, and five commandants down was called the "Western Bureau," while Attendant Cavalier was the "Eastern Bureau."

units.en: Intendant of Danyang.
units.literal: Intendant of Danyang.

units.en: His rank stood below the nine ministers.
units.literal: Ranked below the Nine Ministers.

units.en: Grand tutor of the heir apparent.
units.literal: Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

units.en: Junior tutor.
units.literal: Junior Tutor.

units.en: The household appointed an aide, merit clerk, five officers, and registrar.
units.literal: The household office appointed an aide, merit clerk, five officers, and registrar.

units.en: Director of the heir apparent's household.
units.literal: Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.

units.en: The household office appointed one aide and below.
units.literal: The household office appointed one aide and below.

units.en: Crown prince's chief of ritual standards and timekeeping.
units.literal: Crown Prince's Chief of Ritual Standards and Timekeeping.

units.en: Crown prince's director of the household.
units.literal: Crown Prince's Director of the Household.

units.en: An aide was appointed.
units.literal: An aide was appointed.

units.en: Crown prince's master of servants.
units.literal: Crown Prince's Master of Servants.

units.en: Crown prince's gate masters.
units.literal: Crown Prince's Gate Masters.

units.en: Crown prince's attendants-in-ordinary.
units.literal: Crown Prince's Attendants-in-Ordinary.

units.en: Crown prince's secretariat attendants.
units.literal: Crown Prince's Secretariat Attendants.

units.en: Crown prince's groom.
units.literal: Crown Prince's Groom.

units.en: Crown prince's household attendants.
units.literal: Crown Prince's Household Attendants.

units.en: Crown prince's left and right guard commandants, one each.
units.literal: Crown Prince's Left and Right Guard Commandants, one each.

units.zh: 太子翊軍步兵屯騎三校尉。
units.en: Crown prince's supporting army, footsoldiers, and escort cavalry commandants.
units.literal: Crown Prince's Supporting Army, Footsoldiers, and Escort Cavalry commandants.

units.en: Crown prince's travel tiger guard captain, one person.
units.literal: Crown Prince's Travel Tiger Guard Captain, one person.

units.en: Crown prince's left and right strong crossbow generals.
units.literal: Crown Prince's Left and Right Strong Crossbow Generals.

units.zh: 太子殿中將軍、員外殿中將軍。
units.en: Crown prince's palace-hall general and supernumerary palace-hall general.
units.literal: Crown Prince's Palace-Hall General and supernumerary Palace-Hall General.

units.en: Crown prince's director of the granary office.
units.literal: Crown Prince's Director of the Granary Office.

units.en: Crown prince's director of the constant-following tiger guard.
units.literal: Crown Prince's Director of the Constant-Following Tiger Guard.

units.en: On the right: Eastern Palace staff.
units.literal: On the right: Eastern Palace staff.

units.en: Provincial governors and inspectors.
units.literal: Provincial governors and inspectors.

units.zh: 魏、晉世州牧隆重，刺史任重者爲使持節都督，輕者爲持節督，起漢從帝時，御史中丞馮赦討九江賊，督揚、徐二州軍事，而何、徐《宋志》云起魏武遣諸州將督軍，王珪之《職儀》云起光武，竝非也。
units.en: Under Wei and Jin, provincial governors were honored posts; inspectors with heavy responsibility became commissioners bearing the staff of authority and military overseers, lighter ones commissioners bearing the staff and supervisors. The office began under Emperor Shun of Han, when Censor-in-chief Feng She campaigned against Jiujiang bandits and directed Yang and Xu military affairs; but He and Xu's Song Treatise dates it to Cao Cao's dispatch of provincial generals to oversee troops, and Wang Guizhi's Protocol of Offices dates it to Emperor Guangwu—all are mistaken.
units.literal: In Wei and Jin times provincial governors were weighty; inspectors with heavy duty became commissioners bearing the staff of authority and overseers, lighter ones commissioners bearing the staff of authority and supervisors. It began in the time of Emperor Shun of Han, when Censor-in-chief Feng She suppressed bandits in Jiujiang and oversaw military affairs in Yang and Xu provinces; yet He and Xu's Song Treatise says it began when Cao Cao sent generals of the provinces to oversee armies, and Wang Guizhi's Protocol of Offices says it began with Guangwu—all are wrong.

units.zh: 晉太康中，都督知軍事，刺史治民，各用人。
units.en: In Jin Taikang the military overseer commanded troops and the inspector governed the people, each with separate staffs.
units.literal: In Jin Taikang, the overseer handled military affairs and the inspector governed the people; each had his own appointees.

units.zh: 惠帝末，乃幷任，非要州則單爲刺史。
units.en: By the end of Emperor Hui the two offices were combined; save in a vital province, a man held the inspectorate alone.
units.literal: At the end of Emperor Hui's reign the two posts were merged; unless it was a key province, one person alone served as regional inspector.

units.zh: 州朝置別駕、治中、議曹、文學祭酒、諸曹部從事史。
units.en: At every provincial court stood a chief administrator, a registrar, a deliberation bureau, a libationer of letters and learning, and the section clerks of the various departments.
units.literal: Each province had a chief administrator, registrar, deliberation office, libationer of letters and literature, and section clerks for the various departments.

units.en: Commandant Protecting the Southern Barbarians.
units.literal: Commandant Protecting the Southern Barbarians.

units.en: Its headquarters had assistant clerks.
units.literal: The headquarters had assistant clerks.

units.en: It was under Jing Province.
units.literal: It was subordinate to Jing Province.

units.en: It was abolished at the end of the Jin and Song.
units.literal: It was abolished at the end of Jin and Song.

units.en: In the first year of Jianyuan it was restored, and in the third year abolished.
units.literal: In Jianyuan year 1 it was restored; in year 3 it was abolished.

units.en: It was established in the first year of Yanxing and abolished in Jianwu.
units.literal: It was established in Yanxing year 1 and abolished in Jianwu.

units.en: Commandant Protecting the Three Ba.
units.literal: Commandant Protecting the Three Ba.

units.en: Established in Song.
units.literal: Established in Song.

units.en: In the second year of Jianyuan the post was retitled regional inspector.
units.literal: In Jianyuan year 2, it was changed to regional inspector.

units.en: Pacifying the Barbarians Commandant.
units.literal: Pacifying the Barbarians Commandant.

units.en: Its headquarters also kept assistant clerks, under Yong Province.
units.literal: The headquarters also had assistant clerks, subordinate to Yong Province.

units.en: Pacifying Barbarians Commandant.
units.literal: Pacifying Barbarians Commandant.

units.en: Established in Yongming 3, subordinate to Yi Province.
units.literal: Established in Yongming year 3, subordinate to Yi Province.

units.en: Garrisoning Barbarians Commandant.
units.literal: Garrisoning Barbarians Commandant.

units.en: Subordinate to Ning Province.
units.literal: Subordinate to Ning Province.

units.en: Commandant Protecting the Western Rong.
units.literal: Commandant Protecting the Western Rong.

units.en: Commandant Protecting the Qiang.
units.literal: Commandant Protecting the Qiang.

units.en: These four commandants; posts for the four quarters were set up as well.
units.literal: These four commandants; offices for the four quarters were also established.

units.en: General of the Household Pacifying the Yue.
units.literal: General of the Household Pacifying the Yue.

units.en: Its headquarters had assistant clerks, under Guang Province.
units.literal: The headquarters had assistant clerks, subordinate to Guang Province.

units.en: Commandery administrators and interior ministers.
units.literal: Commandery administrators and interior ministers.

units.en: District magistrates and chancellors.
units.literal: District magistrates and chancellors.

units.en: Where a commandery or district was a princedom, the posts were interior minister and chancellor.
units.literal: Where commanderies and districts were princedoms, the offices were interior minister and chancellor.

units.en: Army Protector Garrisoning the Barbarians.
units.literal: Army Protector Garrisoning the Barbarians.

units.en: Army Protector Pacifying the Distance.
units.literal: Army Protector Pacifying the Distance.

units.en: Miscellaneous titles of Jin times; many were borne by men who headed their commanderies.
units.literal: Miscellaneous titles of the Jin era; many were held by commandery administrators.

units.en: Each prince had one teacher, one friend, and one literary adviser.
units.literal: For each prince: one teacher, one friend, and one man of letters.

units.zh: 國官郎中令、中尉、大農爲三卿，左右常侍、侍郎，上軍、中軍、下軍三軍，典書、典祠、學官、典衞四令，食官、廄牧長、謁者以下。
units.en: A princedom kept a Director of the Palace, a Commandant, and a Grand Agronomist as its three ministers; left and right regular attendants and gentlemen-attendants; upper, middle, and lower armies; directors of documents, sacrifices, the academic office, and the guard; and below them the director of food, the chief of stables and pastures, ushers, and the rest.
units.literal: Princedom offices: the Director of the Palace, the Commandant, and the Grand Agronomist as three ministers; left and right regular attendants and gentlemen-attendants; upper, middle, and lower armies as three armies; directors of documents, sacrifices, the academic office, and the guard as four directors; director of food, chief of stables and pastures, ushers, and below.

units.en: Dukes and marquises kept only the Director of the Palace as their single minister.
units.literal: For dukes and marquises, only the Director of the Palace as one minister.

units.zh: 贊曰：百司分置，惟皇命職。
units.en: In praise: the hundred bureaus stand divided in their stations; only the sovereign fixes their charge.
units.literal: In praise: the hundred offices are set apart in their posts; only the sovereign names their duties.

units.en: Master of Clouds, Recorder of Birds—each keeps its proper measure.
units.literal: Cloud-master and bird-record—each has its proper pattern.
